key_insight: QISS uses low-order correlators from shallow quantum circuits as informative statistics to classically generate strong combinatorial optimization candidates, rather than relying on the quantum circuit to directly sample solutions.
engineering_relevance: This shifts near-term quantum optimization toward error-tolerant measurement of local observables and scalable classical post-processing, making the approach more practical on noisy hardware.
method: Measure low-weight correlators from shallow QAOA-style circuits.
Use the correlator statistics to guide classical candidate generation, independent of the specific optimization objective.
Optionally warm-start QAOA to further improve solution quality.
evidence_signal: On Maximum Cut and Maximum Independent Set, only O(N) low-order correlators were enough to produce competitive solutions, and for 3-regular MaxCut, QISS from p=3 correlators outperformed vanilla QAOA at p=17 on average; the method was also validated on the 54-qubit IQM Emerald device.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and stability of measured correlators, so hardware noise, limited circuit depth, and scaling of classical post-processing remain key implementation concerns.
paper_title: Quantum-informed surrogate sampling for combinatorial optimization
